verdicts.justification: Weighing both merits and drawbacks reflects genuine argumentative balance and reasoning quality.

verdicts.justification: Explicitly naming the scope or failure condition of one's own claim is a substantive epistemic-rigor property.

verdicts.justification: Stock/coalition/template language is a coordination and textual-recurrence fingerprint of production rather than substance, and recycled campaign text plausibly signals less original content rather than genuinely better work.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Mere presence of personal circumstances or identity is a self-reference/topic marker distinct from whether that experience strengthens the argument, though the same lived experience can plausibly also ground genuinely substantive first-hand evidence.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Visible titles and credentials are a producer-identity fingerprint rather than argument substance, but credentialed, well-resourced authors plausibly also tend to produce substantively better comments.

verdicts.label: incidental

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: OCR corruption and typographical noise is a pure production/scanning artifact explicitly disclaimed as unrelated to writer competence or quality.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Requires claims to be concretely grounded in the filer's own direct operational experience, which is substantive evidentiary support.
